prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The first three frames place the refrigerator interior about 0.2–1.0 m in front of the camera wearer, with the door edge and the wearer’s hand/forearm nearest at roughly 0.1–0.4 m; shelves and containers lie farther behind and are partly occluded by the door. By frames 4–5, the view turns away from the refrigerator into the kitchen: nearby counter edges and the wearer’s arm are within about 0.2–0.8 m, while the oven, opposite counters, and standing person are roughly 2–4 m away. The person remains beyond arm’s reach, near the back counter and to the right/front of the wearer, while objects on that counter are within the person’s reach and generally more than 2 m from the wearer. Brightness makes near surfaces and foreground occlusions easier to separate than in RGB, but absolute metre estimates are uncertain, the map blurs object boundaries, and some distant surfaces have inconsistent brightness across frames.
descriptions.segmentation: Frames 1–3 segment the large refrigerator region directly ahead, while the open door and camera wearer’s close hand partly block the interior; the refrigerator is approximately 0.2–1.0 m away and its contents are layered behind the door and shelves. In frames 4–5, masks distinguish the oven, sink, bottles, bowls/cups, and one or more person-labelled regions: the main standing person is roughly 2–4 m ahead near the rear counter, with the oven to that person’s left and the sink and small vessels farther right. The small counter objects are close to one another and within the standing person’s arm-scale vicinity, but not within the camera wearer’s reach; the wearer’s foreground body/arm occupies or occludes parts of the lower view. The map reveals object identities and separations that are ambiguous in the blurred RGB, but it appears unreliable where the refrigerator is labelled as an oven, where person masks are fragmented or duplicated, and where thin or partially visible objects disappear between frames.
descriptions.pose: A magenta hand skeleton appears in the first frame about 0.2–0.5 m away, left/front of the camera wearer against the open refrigerator, making the hand’s spread fingers and reach direction clearer than in RGB; it disappears when occluded or outside the pose detector’s view in frames 2–4. A yellow body skeleton appears in the final frame on the left side of that frame, approximately 2–4 m ahead near the back counter, standing mostly upright and seen approximately side-on, with one arm bent forward; the body faces generally toward the counter/left rather than squarely toward the camera. The skeleton suggests that nearby counter items are within that person’s reach, whereas the person is well beyond the wearer’s arm span, and the lower body is partly obscured by the scene or poorly detected. Pose adds limb configuration and coarse facing direction, but it provides no dependable gaze direction or metric depth, misses the person in an earlier visible frame, and the sparse hand/body detections make motion across all five frames uncertain.
